name: Crude cobalt hydroxide production; at plant
description: The functional unit for this model is one kilogram of crude cobalt hydroxide with a cobalt ore content of 35% and a copper content of 0.47%. The technical scope includes the gate-to-gate production of crude cobalt hydroxide. The system boundary includes incoming transport, hydrometallurgical ore processing, and disposal of process wastes. The material and energy flows data for hydrometallurgical ore processing were based on operations from the following companies: Kamoto, Tenke Fungurume Mining, and Hanrui Cobalt. A process yield of 80% for cobalt was assumed in this study for the ore processing stage.

processDocumentation.timeDescription: This unit process is representative of operations from 2007-2017. Data are applicable over the next 10 years after 2017, i.e., 2027.
processDocumentation.geographyDescription: This unit process is representative of average cobalt ore processing in Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).
processDocumentation.technologyDescription:
The mined copper-cobalt ore is sent to a hydrometallurgical plant for processing. After going through a milling process at the plant, the ore is converted into an enriched concentrate by flotation. 
Concentrate containing sulfides needs to undergo sulfatizing roasting or pressure oxidation first, which converts sulfides into more soluble oxides, before the concentrate can enter the leaching tank, whereas concentrate containing oxides can be fed to the leaching step directly. 
SO2 gas produced from the ore roasting or oxidation processes is a resource to the cobalt producers, and is captured and subsequently converted into sulfuric acid in the onsite acid plant.
In addition, the production of sulfuric acid from sulfur is an exothermic process. The heat released from the process can be harvested to produce steam or electricity, to partially satisfy the energy requirement of the hydrometallurgical plant.
Besides sulfuric acid, SO2 gas is also added to the leaching tank to facilitate the leaching process, by converting Co3+ into soluble Co2+. The leached slurry then undergoes several solvent extraction and stripping steps, which further increase the concentrations of copper and cobalt, and separate them out as a copper-rich solution and a cobalt-rich solution.
The cobalt-rich solution goes through a few precipitation steps to remove iron, aluminum, and manganese impurities, and to recover contained copper. In the end, cobalt is precipitated out as Co(OH)2 by reacting with magnesium oxide (MgO).
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: A process yield of 80% for cobalt was assumed in this study for the ore processing stage.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: Elementary flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. Technosphere flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. The mass balance for this process was not calculated.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: The material and energy flows data for hydrometallurgical ore processing was based on operations at Kamoto, Tenke Fungurume Mining, and a project by Hanrui Cobalt, DRC.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: A process yield of 80% for Co was assumed in this study for the ore processing stage.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: The system boundary includes incoming transport, hydrometallurgical ore processing, and disposal of process wastes. The material and energy data for hydrometallurgical ore processing were based on operations at Kamoto, TFM, and a project by Hanrui Cobalt DRC. Uncertainty was not calculated.

sources.name: Cobalt Life Cycle Analysis Update for the GREET® Model, 2018

reviews.details: Independent internal review was performed by Argonne National Lab.

processDocumentation.intendedApplication: Situation C1 - Accounting, with system-external interactions - The intended application is a purely descriptive accounting / documentation of the analysed system including existing interactions with other systems in the LCI model. The target audience of this model includes LCA practitioners, industry, and the general public. The direct emissions associated with this dataset come from GREET which considers greenhouse gases, water consumption, and criteria air pollutants, including VOCs, carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides, particulate matter, and sulfur oxides. Therefore, the following TRACI impact categories are compatible with this dataset: global warming potential, smog formation, and human health – particulate matter. It may be compatible with additional impact categories.
processDocumentation.projectDescription: This project was funded by DOE. These data are cradle-to-gate LCIs for the production of refined cobalt and cobalt chemicals by production stages, which was an update for the GREET model, 2018.

publication.name: Cobalt Life Cycle Analysis Update for the GREET® Model, 2018
